topic: Beryllium-copper handling: NGK Metals Copper Beryllium Wrought Alloys SDS (includes alloy 25, C17200)
citation: NGK Metals Corporation. Copper Beryllium Wrought Alloys, Safety Data Sheet according to the Hazard Communication Standard (HazCom 2012), version 1.0, issue and revision date 16 January 2023.
task_or_setup: Hazards, exposure operations, limits and controls
participants_or_bench: not applicable
key_quantitative_findings: S2.1: 'Metallic product which poses little or no immediate hazard in solid form. Exposure ... can occur when melting, casting, dross handling, pickling, chemical cleaning, heat treating, abrasive cutting, welding, grinding, sanding, polishing, milling, crushing, or otherwise heating or abrading the surface of this material in a manner which generates particulate.' GHS classes include Resp. Sens. 1, Carc. 1A, Repr. 1B, STOT RE 1. S8.1: OSHA PEL (TWA) 0.2 ug/m3 and OSHA PEL (Ceiling) 2 ug/m3 for beryllium. S8.2: 'Ensure good ventilation of the work station. If applicable, use process enclosures, local exhaust ventilation or other engineering controls...'. Product codes include 25 (C17200).
limitations: Generic for wrought alloys; soldering is not named in the list; the SDS of the wire actually bought takes precedence
relevance_to_design: Bench rules for cutting, joining, heat treating and cleaning C17200 wire (DEC-063; DEC-097 proposed)
design_implication: Buy aged wire; shear-cut; no pickling, abrasive cutting or welding; solder under local exhaust; bag offcuts
